Calamartigaṇḍa (CITD), Telugu-Kannaḍa; a title of the Kākatīya kings; from Kannaḍa gaṇḍa meaning ‘the husband, lord, master,’ i. e. ‘one who can control or punish’, and Telugu calam meaning ‘obstinacy, rudeness, overbearing’; translated^1 as ‘one who is the controller or punisher of spiteful men or men of overbearing conduct’.
[1] Correction submitted by Dr. Sampada Savardekar on 20210207. Reference: https://github.com/sanskrit-lexicon/csl-corrections/issues/51.
cālī (IA 15), a system of land revenue.

calivaṃdīli, caliveṃdala, caliveṃdra, calipaṃdili (CITD), Telugu-Kannaḍa; halting place for travellers, where they are supplied gratis with milk and whey^1 or with water.
[1] Correction submitted by Dr. Sampada Savardekar on 20210207. Reference: https://github.com/sanskrit-lexicon/csl-corrections/issues/51.
catuḥ-sīm-āvacchinna , same as sva-sīm-āvachinna, catur-aghāṭa-viśuddha, etc. Cf. Majumdar, Ins. Beng., Vol. III, p. 125.
